mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05), or the mean FEDFUNDS reverts within 3 months without a sustained return to expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as labor market strength boosts investor confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows meeting the trigger, SPX forward returns are negative or flat, and the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE change and SPX return is not statistically significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average, without a corresponding spike in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as it signals robust business demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO._12mo moving average AND CPIAUCSL < CPIAUCSL._12mo moving average
failure_condition: Over 5 days after the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative, and the short-term (5-day) correlation between INDPRO/CPIAUCSL change and SPX return is < 0.2 in absolute value.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a sustained drop in consumer confidence proxy (HOUST) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as weak supply signals impending economic softening.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 60 days following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1), or INDPRO recovers without a corresponding rebound in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as it signals a potential recessionary turn and tighter financial conditions.
failure_condition: During the 20-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1), or UNRATE reverts below 5.5% within 1 month without a subsequent SPX rebound.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising payrolls (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in CPIAUCSL suggests wage growth is not inflationary, and this combination predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as it reinforces labor market strength without price pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases month-over-month for 2 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL remains flat or falls over the same period
failure_condition: In 5 days after the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative, and the short-term (5-day) regression coefficient between PAYEMS/CPIAUCSL change and SPX return is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in retail sales proxy (not available in the given catalog; fallback to HOUST as a demand proxy) followed by a rebound above trend predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as it signals a bottom in demand weakness.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < HOUST._12mo moving average AND HOUST > HOUST._12mo moving average in the following month
failure_condition: Over 20 days after the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive, or the pattern of decline followed by rebound in HOUST is not statistically associated with SPX returns (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding decline in industrial production (INDPRO), predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as it suggests disinflation without supply shock.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO does not decline over the same period
failure_condition: In 60 days following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1), or CPIAUCSL reverts upward while INDPRO continues to decline.
